About us

A group of Christians and one conviction: the heart of Elohim turns toward the weakest.

Our story in a few words

The Christian association La Paix du Cœur / Kimia Na Motema is a work inspired by the Lord Yehoshua (Jesus), carried by a group of Christians moved by the love of Elohim and by compassion for people in need. We work humbly and selflessly, for the glory of Elohim alone. Founded in 2014 in Montréal, Canada, this vision was born to bring support and hope to orphans.

Our mission

By the grace of the Lord, the Provider and the Rewarder of those who seek him, the Christian association La Paix du Cœur exists to reveal to the nations the Heart of the Lord, turned toward the weakest: widows and widowers, orphans, the poor and the homeless, regardless of language, colour or race. Working in a spirit of love and service, this non-profit Christian association offers everything free of charge, for the glory of Elohim alone.

Why “Kimia Na Motema”?

“Kimia na motema” means “peace of the heart” in Lingala, a language spoken in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of the Congo. The name honours the roots of part of our community and the peace we want to offer: not a life without hardship, but a heart that is comforted and accompanied.

Love

Serving as Yehoshua (Jesus) served, expecting nothing in return.

Humility

Working quietly, for the glory of Elohim alone.

Dignity

Seeing each person as made in God’s image, never as a case.

Self-reliance

Helping today so that everyone can stand on their own tomorrow.

Our programmes

  1. Support for people in need

    Food, clothing, financial and spiritual help for people going through hard times.

  2. Training workshops

    Workshops, seminars, talks and awareness campaigns that help people become self-reliant.

  3. Helping other charities

    Supporting other associations that carry social and humanitarian projects.

Our ethical storytelling charter

  • We show resilience and joy, never pity.
  • No child’s face is published without the written consent of a parent or guardian.
  • We use first names only, sometimes changed, and never an exact location.
  • The people we help read their story before it is published and can withdraw it at any time.
  • When a photo isn’t possible, we prefer a hand-made illustration.
